Lul Tim Predicted At Least 1 Person Will Snitch in Lil Durk's Murder-for-Hire Case (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, we revisit Lul Tim discussing the possibility that someone could become an informant in the murder-for-hire case involving rapper Lil Durk. Tim explored the complexities of street justice versus relying on law enforcement, highlighting the moral and ethical dilemmas that can come with taking matters into your own hands.

DJ Vlad expanded on the potential fallout of retaliatory violence, noting that the consequences can extend beyond those directly involved and impact loved ones left without fathers and partners who are incarcerated. The conversation also touched on broader conflicts in the rap scene, including the Lil Durk and NBA YoungBoy beef, and the significant losses suffered on both sides.

recentItems.title: Judge Mathis Reacts to Getting His Keefe D "Not Guilty" Prediction Wrong (Part 1)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
-------
Judge Mathis returns to VladTV to address why his “not guilty” call in the Keefe D trial didn’t match the jury’s guilty verdict. Speaking as a former Detroit criminal defense attorney and longtime judge, Mathis breaks down “beyond a reasonable doubt,” jury instructions, possible appeal issues, and how evidence like Keefe D’s book and VladTV footage played into the case tied to Tupac Shakur’s murder. He also discusses race, gang stereotypes, Southside Crips, hip hop culture, and why jurors may view defendants differently in court. The conversation expands into the Lil Durk murder trial, with analysis of OTF Jam, OTF Vonnie, King Von, disputed testimony, witness credibility, and defense strategy. Mathis also references Malcolm X, government surveillance concerns, and the challenges facing high-profile defendants in America’s legal system.

Kodak Black's Lawyer Bradford Cohen on How He Got Kodak Pardoned by Trump (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/K7__iCx2ghE
--------

Defense attorney Bradford Cohen joins VladTV to break down his long history representing Kodak Black, from early probation violations as a teenager to the 2019 federal weapons case involving ATF Form 4473 paperwork. Cohen explains why he viewed Kodak’s 46-month sentence as excessive, comparing the charge to the widely discussed Hunter Biden gun case and arguing that similar offenses are often treated differently in federal court.

Cohen also details the campaign that helped secure Kodak’s sentence commutation from President Donald Trump, including media pressure, support from Jake Paul and Lil Pump, and a lawsuit against the Bureau of Prisons over Kodak’s treatment at Big Sandy in Kentucky. The attorney, who first met Trump on The Apprentice, discusses clemency advocacy, Alice Johnson’s work, and the day he picked Kodak up near Chicago before returning to Florida.

recentItems.title: Max B: I Sold My Mom Crack During Harlem’s Crack Era (Part 1)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
Max B returns to VladTV for a rare in-person conversation, reflecting on his childhood in Harlem during New York’s crack era. The rapper opens up about being raised around addiction, including the painful memory of once selling crack to his mother, while describing life near the Abraham Lincoln Houses and the family dysfunction that shaped him.

He also discusses time spent in a structured group home, how his grandmother tried to give him stability, and growing up alongside figures like Cam’ron. Max B shares emotional memories of his late older brother Eric, whose bag of cassette mixtapes—featuring blends, R&B, Frankie Beverly and Maze, Michael Jackson and more—helped lay the foundation for his musical identity.

From Harlem street life to early influences and personal loss, Max B offers a raw look at the experiences that shaped his story.

recentItems.title: Judge Mathis & Vlad Debate if Childhood Sexual Abuse Leads to Violent Adult Crime (Part 9)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 8: https://youtu.be/oyV8U3yvPkw
Part 1: https://youtu.be/lOCPGaKuQxw
--------

Judge Mathis sits down with Vlad for a wide-ranging conversation on mental illness, trauma, and crime in America’s justice system. The discussion begins with Vlad’s interview with John Hinckley Jr., the man found not guilty by reason of insanity after shooting President Ronald Reagan while obsessed with Jodie Foster, and how the case influenced insanity laws and the Brady Bill.

Mathis compares Hinckley’s confinement to the ongoing Lindsey Clancy case, raising questions about psychiatric treatment versus prison. The conversation then turns to county jails, Detroit, federal penitentiaries, and Mathis’ view that poor communities often criminalize mental illness instead of providing counseling.

Vlad and Mathis also debate whether childhood sexual abuse can contribute to violent adult behavior, referencing Clark Fredericks, the Boy Scouts abuse scandal, prison culture, revenge, and accountability. The interview closes with reflections on street violence, Tupac, Baby Lane, and how trauma shapes decisions.

DJ Vlad addresses his escalating feud with N.O.R.E. after the Drink Champs host called into Hot 97 with new criticism. He also responds to N.O.R.E.’s comments about Black and Latino guests on VladTV, explains why he keeps his relationships and children off social media, and rejects the idea that he should pause posting interviews with Black or Latino figures.

The discussion moves through Drink Champs, Revolt, Diddy, Yung Miami, Lamar Odom, Bad Bunny, Joe Budden, Charlamagne Tha God, DJ Akademiks, The Source, and Jordan Brand. Vlad challenges N.O.R.E. to address allegations about pressuring guests to drink, take a lie detector test, or sue for defamation if the claims are false.
